messages:
Anya: Quick sync — need to decide prioritization approach for next quarter. We have two competing asks: API ergonomics (SDK polish, streaming stability, clearer rate limits) vs Console features (route dashboards, rollout UI, RBAC). Customers are loudly API-first, PMs want Console completeness. Proposal: pick a prioritization framework (RICE vs impact/effort) and define launch criteria for each surface. Thoughts?

Mike: +1 on picking a framework. From eng POV API wins for short-term PLG lift. Smaller scope changes (streaming retry, SDK docs) give high ROI. Suggest we run a lightweight RICE for top 6 bets. Example quick calc I did: 
```
R=8 (monthly users affected)
I=6 (how much it moves activation)
C=4 (confidence)
E=3 (months)
RICE = (8*6*4)/3 = 64
```
This helps compare across different shapes (Console tickets are big E but large R sometimes).

Jia: DevEx: Console improvements reduce onboarding support and make success team happier. Impact is less immediate for PLG but matters for retention. For Console launches we should require measurable acceptance criteria: onboarding completion rate >= 70%, time-to-first-success <= 10m, and < 0.5 support tickets per 100 new accounts in first 30 days. Those are easy to instrument.

Sam: Sales: Enterprise customers repeatedly ask for better rollout UI and RBAC. That's directly revenue-driving for Dedicated/Private deals — longer sales cycles but higher ACV. We should tag those Console items as "enterprise pull" and treat them as sales-influenced backlog that can be scheduled alongside API work. If we ignore, we'll lose a few deals.

Ben: High-level suggestion: use RICE for PLG/PL area (API-first) because it normalizes reach and confidence. Use a separate "Contracted/Enterprise" priority lane for Console features tied to revenue/commitments and use slot-based sequencing (reserve 20% of eng capacity for enterprise work). Also require a minimal launch checklist for anything shipped to Console: docs, telemetry, rollback plan, and guardrails for data residency when applicable.

Mike: Small practical note — when we compute RICE, make sure Reach uses MAU or number of active routes; Impact should map to expected pct delta (0.1/0.3/0.5) not vague words. I can add a tiny spreadsheet to standardize scoring. @Jia @Anya can you add the acceptance metrics into that sheet? :thumbsup:

Jia: Yup I’ll add the onboarding KPIs and a checklist column for Console readiness.

Anya: OK next steps: 1) Monday 30m RICE scoring session (prod + eng + devex + sales) 2) Mike to attach quick spreadsheet with scoring normalization 3) Jia to add Console acceptance criteria into sheet 4) Ben to confirm capacity reservation for enterprise lane. We'll sequence API-first wins that unlock PLG activation while preserving slots for enterprise Console work. Thanks everyone.

Anya: Appreciate it — please post the sheet link in #product and I'll book the slot.
